get.summary: Gets the latest or a given revision E-Form.
get.description:
Specify `revisionId` to retrieve a specific idempotent revision of the E-Form. Otherwise, the latest revision will be retrieved.
Returns `404` NotFound if there is not an E-Form rendition for the specified document or no such specified revision for the E-Form.

parameters.name: revisionId
parameters.description: The unique id for the E-Form Revision.

dataType.description:
Describes the type of data represented by the keyword type or field definition.

`Numeric9` represents a number up to 9 digits in length.

`Numeric20` represents a number up to 20 digits in length.

`Alphanumeric` represents any value with letters and/or numbers.

`Currency` represents a monetary value.

`Date` represents a date.

`DateTime` represents both a date and a time.

`Decimal` represents a high-precision decimal value (128-bit).

`FloatingPoint` represents numeric values that have variable decimal
 point locations.

`Boolean` represents a true or false value

Problem-Detail.description: The Problem Detail format defines a way to carry machine-readable details of errors in a HTTP response to avoid the need to define new error response formats for HTTP APIs. Problem details can be extended and defined for specific problem types.

type.description:
An absolute URI that identifies the problem type.  When
dereferenced, it should provide human-readable documentation
for the problem type (e.g., using HTML).

title.description:
A short, human-readable summary of the problem type. It should
not change from occurrence to occurrence of the problem.

status.description:
The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this
occurrence of the problem.

detail.description:
A human readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the
problem.

instance.description:
A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of
the problem.  It may or may not yield further information
if dereferenced.

Accept-Language.name: Accept-Language
Accept-Language.description: The Accept-Language header field can be used by user agents to indicate the set of natural languages that are preferred in the response. Language tags are defined in RFC 5646. If none of the languages given are supported, a default language will be returned.

Content-Language.description:
The Content-Language header field describes the natural language(s)
of the intended audience for the representation.  Note that this
might not be equivalent to all the languages used within the
representation.

Reference: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.3.2
